visual_system_craft.critique: The visual system suffers from a lack of unified geometry and inconsistent component grammar. The 'Start Adventure' button uses a pill shape (full radius), while the 'Options' button and the stat cards use a small, inconsistent border radius, creating a disjointed UI language. The 'Controls' panel on the right is visually broken: the 'Move' label is clipped by the arrow icon, and the key bindings (Z, X, Arrows) lack a defined container or background, making them look like floating artifacts rather than a cohesive component. The typography lacks a strict scale; the 'Level 1-1' header uses a wide, tracked-out sans-serif that clashes with the condensed, glowing title font. Furthermore, the 'Neon Valley' selector and 'Controls' panel use a flat, dark fill that lacks the glassmorphism or texture present in the stat cards, breaking the material consistency. The alignment of the left-hand stat stack is loose, and the 'Hearts' icon is significantly smaller than the 'Coins' and 'Star' icons, disrupting the visual rhythm.
visual_system_craft.suggestion: 1. Unify the UI Geometry: Adopt a single border-radius system (e.g., 12px for cards, 24px for buttons) to ensure all interactive elements feel like part of the same family. 2. Fix the Controls Component: Encapsulate the key bindings in distinct, styled 'keycap' containers with a subtle stroke or shadow to separate them from the background. Fix the 'Move' label collision by increasing the panel width or adjusting the icon placement. 3. Standardize Typography: Apply a consistent font weight and tracking to the 'Level 1-1' header to match the hierarchy of the main title. Ensure the 'Options' button text matches the weight of the 'Start' button. 4. Harmonize Materials: Apply a consistent background treatment (e.g., semi-transparent dark glass with a subtle border) to the 'Controls' and 'Sector' panels to match the 'Stat' cards on the left. 5. Refine Iconography: Resize the 'Hearts' icon to match the visual weight of the other stat icons and ensure all icons share the same stroke width and style.
